To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the mechanical performance of composites is strongly influenced by the fibre orientation in the moulding.
the structure/performance relationship in injection molded composite moldings can be described as follows: The structure of the moldings depends on the processing conditions and on the system used.
the structure of the composite is determined by the matrix, the fibre and the processing conditions and this structure governs the mechanical properties of the composite.
In summary, our research is concerned with

a) the development of novel experimental techniques to characterize composite materials in terms of their through-thickness properties, b) the development of a theoretical model to predict the mechanical properties of composite materials in the through-thickness direction, c) a study of the relationship between the structure and properties of composites, d) the development of processing conditions to control the structure and properties, e) the application of the above to the design and manufacture of composite components.
the development of a new generation of injection moulding techniques which can be applied to the processing of fibre reinforced composites with a view to improving their mechanical properties.

the development of an understanding of the structure/property relationship in injection molded composite parts and with the development of new experimental methods for the characterization of the structure.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the Dynamic mode is the preferred method for injection molding of composites, since it produces a more regular structure with improved mechanical properties, and that the 'Rebound technique' is a very promising method for the characterization of composites.
the Dynamic mode is the preferred molding technique for injection molding of composites.
the structure and properties of injection molded composites can be controlled by appropriate processing conditions.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

a) the Dynamic mode produces more regular fibre orientation than the Static mode, b) the fibre orientation in Dynamic mode is more regular in the PP/g system than in the PNc, c) the Dynamic mode in PP/g is more regular in transverse direction than the Static mode.
the'rebound' test is capable of giving a quick and reliable estimate of the in-plane properties of composites.
the 'wafers technique' is an effective means for studying the through-thickness aspects in composites.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the structure/performance of composites is strongly influenced by the moulding regime and that this can be exploited for the development of new composite materials.
the through-thickness properties can be predicted by the use of simple models.

a) the mechanical properties of composites are strongly dependent on the processing conditions and b) that the'rebound method' can be used as an effective tool for evaluation of the mechanical properties of composite moldings in both longitudinal and transverse directions.
